prompt: Which exported variable sends the requests `gcloud storage` makes to fake-gcs-server instead of to Google?
hint: One of them names an address.

choices.text: `CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT`
choices.why: That names the project the request acts in, `planner-dev`; the address is still Google's.

choices.text: `CLOUDSDK_API_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES_STORAGE`
choices.why: Right. It replaces Cloud Storage's address with `http://localhost:4443/storage/v1/` for `gcloud`.

choices.text: `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST`, which every Google tool reads
choices.why: That one is read by the Python client library. `gcloud` takes its endpoint from its own setting.

choices.text: `CLOUDSDK_AUTH_DISABLE_CREDENTIALS`
choices.why: That stops `gcloud` sending credentials; it does not say where the request goes.

prompt: Why does the lab set `CLOUDSDK_AUTH_DISABLE_CREDENTIALS=true` in every terminal, when the emulator checks no credentials anyway?
hint: Think of a terminal that has lost its endpoint line.

choices.text: Because fake-gcs-server refuses every request that arrives carrying a token, a key or a signature
choices.why: It accepts anything; the lesson's `curl` read an object with no credentials at all.

choices.text: So a terminal that reaches Google by mistake has nothing of yours to send
choices.why: Right. Without credentials, a request that escapes to the real address is refused rather than answered as you.

choices.text: Because the Python libraries need it to find the emulator
choices.why: The libraries find the emulator through the `…_EMULATOR_HOST` variables.

choices.text: To make `gcloud` start faster
choices.why: It changes what is sent, not how fast anything starts.

prompt: You stop fake-gcs-server with Ctrl+C at the end of a sitting and start it again the next day. What is in it?
hint: Look at the `-backend` flag.

choices.text: Everything from yesterday, saved on disk in the directory it was started from
choices.why: `-backend memory` keeps nothing on disk.

choices.text: Nothing at all
choices.why: Right. Each lesson rebuilds what it needs from its first command.

choices.text: Yesterday's buckets, empty
choices.why: The buckets are in the same memory as the objects, and go with them.

choices.text: Only what was in `quitanda-raw-prod`, the bucket the lesson used most
choices.why: No bucket is kept; the emulator has no idea which one mattered.

prompt: What does `gcloud config set component_manager/fixed_sdk_version 591.0.0` protect you from?
hint: It is run just before the components are installed.

choices.text: An install that offers to update the whole command line first
choices.why: Right. With it, the version in your terminal stays the one in the transcripts.

choices.text: Downloading the emulators from a mirror somewhere other than Google's own servers
choices.why: Where they come from does not change; what version the command line is does.

choices.text: A Java version that the emulators cannot use
choices.why: Java is the first block's package and has nothing to do with this setting.

choices.text: Running out of disk space halfway while the components are being unpacked
choices.why: It changes no size; the lab is 1.6 GB either way.

prompt: `gcloud storage buckets list` answers `You do not currently have an active account selected`. What is the fix in this lab?
hint: The error suggests a command. Do not run it.

choices.text: Run `gcloud auth login`, as the error suggests, and sign in with your own Google account
choices.why: That signs the command line in to a real Google account, which this course never wants.

choices.text: Restart fake-gcs-server
choices.why: The emulator was never asked; `gcloud` stopped before sending anything.

choices.text: Export `CLOUDSDK_AUTH_DISABLE_CREDENTIALS=true` again
choices.why: Right. It tells `gcloud` to send no credentials, and the request goes out.

choices.text: Set `CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT` to your own project
choices.why: A missing project gives a different error, about the `[project]` property.

prompt: An error says `gcloud crashed (ConnectionError)` with `port=4443` and `Connection refused`. What happened?
hint: Two words in the middle matter more than the first two.

choices.text: The command line is broken and has to be downloaded and installed again from the start
choices.why: `crashed` is how `gcloud` reports a refused connection; nothing is broken.

choices.text: Google received the request and refused it
choices.why: Port 4443 on localhost is the emulator, not Google.

choices.text: Nothing was listening on that port
choices.why: Right. Start fake-gcs-server again in its own terminal.

choices.text: The project is not set
choices.why: That error names the `[project]` property and never reaches the network.

prompt: Starting fake-gcs-server prints `bind: address already in use`. What does that tell you?
hint: Something is already on the port.

choices.text: Another emulator is already answering on 4443
choices.why: Right. There is nothing to fix unless you wanted an empty one; `pgrep -af fake-gcs-server` finds it.

choices.text: The port is blocked by the operating system's firewall, which refuses the program's bind
choices.why: A firewall does not make a port look taken to a program on the same machine.

choices.text: Java is missing
choices.why: fake-gcs-server is a Go program and needs no Java.

choices.text: The `-backend memory` flag is wrong
choices.why: The flag is the lab's own; the error is about the port.

prompt: A bucket created with `--location=us-east1` on the emulator reports `southamerica-east1`. Why?
hint: Look at how the lab starts the emulator.

choices.text: Cloud Storage moves every new bucket to the region nearest to the person who created it
choices.why: Cloud Storage keeps the location you asked for; it is a promise about where the bytes live.

choices.text: It keeps no region per bucket and answers with the one in its start command
choices.why: Right. `-location southamerica-east1` in the fifth block is what it reports for every bucket.

choices.text: `CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT` overrides the location
choices.why: A project has no location of its own, and the variable names only the project.

choices.text: `us-east1` does not exist
choices.why: It exists; the emulator simply does not keep a location per bucket.

prompt: Which of these does this lab have an emulator for?
hint: Four services from Google, one from somebody else.

choices.text: BigQuery
choices.why: There is no BigQuery emulator from Google or anybody else; DuckDB runs the SQL instead.

choices.text: Cloud SQL
choices.why: Nothing imitates the managed service; a local PostgreSQL runs the engine.

choices.text: Pub/Sub
choices.why: Right. It is Google's own emulator, a component of the command line.

choices.text: IAM
choices.why: No control plane has an emulator, IAM included.

prompt: `curl` read an object from fake-gcs-server with no credentials. What does that mean for lesson 4, about who may read a bucket?
hint: Ask what the emulator can refuse.

choices.text: Its refusals are taught from the documentation
choices.why: Right. The emulator allows every request, so nothing here produces a denial.

choices.text: The objects in the lab are public, and should be made private before lesson 4 starts
choices.why: There is no private here to make: the emulator does not check.

choices.text: Cloud Storage also allows anonymous reads by default, so nothing changes
choices.why: Cloud Storage refuses an anonymous read unless the bucket grants one.

choices.text: Lesson 4 has to be done against a real project
choices.why: It is read where it cannot be practised; no lesson requires an account.

prompt: An object's ACL shows `projectOwner-test-project`. What does it tell you?
hint: `planner-dev` is the project the lab uses.

choices.text: The object belongs to a project called test-project in your account
choices.why: There is no account; the name is the emulator's invention.

choices.text: You are talking to the emulator
choices.why: Right. It is the emulator's signature; an ACL naming one of your projects would mean you are not.

choices.text: The project variable was not exported
choices.why: Without a project the command would have failed before reaching anything.

choices.text: The bucket was made public at some point, and anybody may now read the object
choices.why: It names an owner, not a reader.

prompt: Why does this course read prices from the pricing pages rather than from the Cloud Billing Catalog API?
hint: Follow what the API asks for.

choices.text: The API's list trails the pages by a month, so its prices are out of date
choices.why: It is the same list as the pages, for programs.

choices.text: The API has no prices for São Paulo
choices.why: It has every SKU in every region.

choices.text: The API needs a key, so a project, so an account
choices.why: Right. So the pages are read, the date is written down, and nothing unread is shown.

choices.text: The pages are cheaper than the API
choices.why: Both are free to read; the API's requirement is an account.

prompt: Standard storage costs $0.035 per GiB-month in São Paulo. What does one TiB cost for a month there, in dollars?
hint: A TiB is 1,024 GiB.

prompt: A Class B operation costs $0.0004 per thousand. What do a million reads cost, in dollars?
hint: A million is a thousand thousands.

prompt: A pricing page charges storage per GiB-month. What is a GiB?
hint: The `i` matters.

choices.text: 10⁹ bytes
choices.why: That is a GB; a GiB is about 7% larger.

choices.text: 2³⁰ bytes
choices.why: Right. A gibibyte is 1,073,741,824 bytes.
A GiB is 1,024 MiB.

choices.text: Whatever the region defines
choices.why: The unit is the same everywhere; the price per unit is what changes.

prompt: `gcloud storage ls gs://quitanda-raw-prod` printed `gs://quitanda-raw-prod/raw/`, a folder nobody created. Where did it come from?
hint: Look at the `curl` below it.

choices.text: The console creates a folder for every new prefix
choices.why: No console was involved; the bucket holds only three objects.

choices.text: `gcloud storage cp` creates the folders of a path as it uploads
choices.why: It uploaded three objects and nothing else.

choices.text: A grouping of names at the first slash
choices.why: Right. A folder is the answer to a question, and exists only while some name starts with it.

choices.text: fake-gcs-server keeps a directory on disk for every prefix it is given
choices.why: The JSON API answer shows `prefixes`, the grouping, not stored directories.

prompt: A line is appended to a local file and it is uploaded again under the same name. Which of these changes on the object?
hint: Three values were printed before and after.

choices.text: Nothing: the upload is skipped because the name exists
choices.why: The upload ran, and the size went from 64 to 78.

choices.text: Only the size
choices.why: The MD5 and the generation changed too.

choices.text: Size, MD5 and generation: it is a new object
choices.why: Right. Nothing is edited in place; the old bytes are gone unless versioning is on.

choices.text: The name gets a numbered suffix, so the old and the new versions are kept side by side
choices.why: Cloud Storage keeps the name; without versioning the old object is simply replaced.

prompt: Two programs may write the same object. How does one of them avoid overwriting a write it never saw?
hint: Every version of an object has a number.

choices.text: It uploads with the generation it read as a precondition, so the write fails if the object has moved on
choices.why: Right. The same idea as a version column in a table.

choices.text: It renames the object before writing
choices.why: A rename is a copy and a delete, and does nothing to stop the other writer.

choices.text: It checks the folder first
choices.why: There is no folder, and a check followed by a write leaves a window for the other program.

choices.text: It writes a smaller object
choices.why: Size has nothing to do with who wins.

prompt: Which of these bucket names follows the course's scheme and Cloud Storage's rules?
hint: Company, layer, environment, and no dots.

choices.text: `quitanda.raw.prod`
choices.why: A dotted name needs a verified domain and breaks the TLS certificate of the usual address.

choices.text: `Quitanda-Raw-Prod`
choices.why: Capital letters are refused, by the emulator and by Cloud Storage.

choices.text: `raw-prod-ana`
choices.why: No company, and a person's name, who will move while the bucket stays.

choices.text: `quitanda-curated-prod`
choices.why: Right: company, layer, environment, all lowercase.

prompt: Daily files are written under `raw/orders/dt=2026-10-01/`, because a year-month-day date lists in ___ order.
hint: Alphabetical order of these strings is the same as another order.

prompt: Put in order what a new terminal needs before `gcloud storage buckets list` answers from the emulator.
hint: The emulator's own terminal comes first.
items: Start fake-gcs-server in a terminal of its own
Put `gcloud` on the path and activate the virtual environment
Export the project and the variable that disables credentials
Export the endpoint overrides and the emulator hosts

hint: Each names a different line of the setup.

pairs.right: The path to the command line

pairs.left: `You do not currently have an active account selected`
`The required property [project] is not currently set`

prompt: A colleague's terminal lists buckets you have never seen, with a project id that is not `planner-dev`. What is the first thing to do?
hint: Think of which half of the trick is missing.

choices.text: Stop and find where the credentials and the endpoint went, before running anything else
choices.why: Right. That terminal is talking to Google as somebody; nothing more should be sent from it until you know who.

choices.text: Restart fake-gcs-server so its buckets go away
choices.why: The emulator would show no strangers' buckets; these came from somewhere else.

choices.text: Delete the unknown buckets
choices.why: They are somebody's real data, and deleting them is the worst possible step.

choices.text: Run `gcloud components install` again
choices.why: The installation is not what changed; the terminal's settings are.
